utterances.text: Really, Mr. Macar, the VRS wasn't created until 21st of May -- or the 12th of May was when it was pronounced and it started on the 21st of May. You weren't aware of Arkan's or Seselj's Men operating in Sarajevo before that? And, thus, they could not have been part of the army because it didn't exist yet.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the Territorial Defence. That, is the people were organised through the TO and their military units defended their territory. Whether there were any Arkan's Men in Sarajevo, I really don't know. Roads were not safe, so it wasn't easy to go from one part of Sarajevo to another at the time, so they may have been present in a part of town. And the army consisted of organised territorial units. They were organised through the staffs of Territorial Defence. And what kind of volunteers there were, that's something I really cannot comment on. Our main concern was, from late April on, to establish the MUP headquarters, create the conditions necessary for that at Vrace, where we were almost cut off from everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, did you never hear of Slavko Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned more about Mr. Slavko Aleksic by following the trial at the ICTY and the information about that in the Bosnian media. Most of what I know originates from this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware he was a member of the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that. There were hundreds of them, so how should I have known by name, by face, or any other way?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There were hundreds of Slavko Aleksics? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the situation that prevailed in late April until the time I left Sarajevo, the name Slavko Aleksic meant nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which trial in the ICTY were you following where you heard about Slavko Aleksic? Was it this one or some other one?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's another case. It could be Seselj or some other. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How many trials have you been following?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did so very rarely. Perhaps before going to bed, I would see a news flash of about a minute or two, but I didn't really follow attentively.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the Slavko Aleksic you heard about is the one who was commanding forces in the front line neighbourhood near the Jewish cemetery in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm under oath, so I must say that I was not familiar with his movements, nor do I know which unit he led. I can say no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see him on the news or in the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he were to walk past me right now, I wouldn't recognise him by face. But I do remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about Batko? Did you hear of a man whose nickname was Batko? Veselin Vlahovic, I think, is his full name.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name Batko is something I remember in -- yes, I heard of Veselin Vlahovic who was arrested in Spain, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just recently, right, in the past year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in 1992, you must have heard about him. He was, in some ways, a one-man crime wave in certain parts of Sarajevo. I think particularly in the Grbavica area. You knew about that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he started a crime wave or not, I don't know. But the MUP, through the public security station, received information from the citizens about Batko's activities. He was said to belong to some military unit, and then the station first informed the military police. After that, I remember that, pursuant to Mr. Planojevic's orders, and after consultations with the minister, attempts were made to arrest him, but a short while before that, the military police arrested him and launched the relevant procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were aware that part of the conflict between Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Stanisic, and, indeed, on Mr. Stanisic's side, Mr. Mandic and Radovan Karadzic, was over Batko and the failure to effectively do anything about him. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment that, but I know that the police did everything necessary, once it received information from the citizens of the area, to arrest Batko. They even informed the military police there. I don't remember what their organisation was like, but I think that it went through the public security station. After some time, and I remember that a larger-scale action was planned, but then before it -- the operation was launched, the military police arrested him, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he was released within ten days and nothing else ever happened to him, in terms of prosecution, until his recent arrest last year; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened to him later, if he was released, or if he escaped, or if he was tried, I don't know, but I know that he was no longer in the area. Quite some time later, it transpired that he had escaped from the military police detention facility, which caused revolt in the police and also among the citizens, Serbs and non-Serbs alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You all right? Can we continue --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm just trying to find the right position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now Exhibit P746. It's tab number 97. If the usher could assist me, I'll hand you the hard copy. It's apparently processed on the 18th of August, 1992. And it's from Colonel Sipcic in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Did you know who Colonel Sipcic was? He was in the VRS in the Sarajevo area.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is familiar, but I don't remember the colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The first paragraph is talking about sniper activity --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I have to object. The first document that you show, I didn't, because I was wondering whether you intend to inquire with the witness, has he ever seen the document. Like you are teaching me during my direct, I now have to obviously remind you that you have to establish whether the witness have seen this document at all, has he read it, and all the other things that you need before you can read from the document. Otherwise, you can pose the question, I guess. That was the -- so far, that was the rulings that I remember in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'll leave it to Their Honours. I don't know that that's necessarily always true. And I will ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. But I see that it says Major-General rather than Colonel Sipcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I -- if I said "colonel," I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen the document and don't know what it contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay of the first paragraph he is talking about activities in Nedzarici, Dobrinje, Grabovica, Rajlovac. In paragraph 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, let him read it and then pose a question, Mr. Hannis. That is what Mr. Zecevic was reminding you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I didn't think it was necessary to have him read the entire document. I wanted to direct him to a specific paragraph and then I'll read that paragraph to him and ask him a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, well, you could direct -- ask him to read only that paragraph to which -- on the basis of which you wish to pose your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's been my practice before now, oftentimes that I will read the paragraph. Is there a problem with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The problem is the -- putting on the record documents which may not become evidence. And that is what we are trying to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this one is P746. It is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's why I was confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But there's one other slight problem, Your Honours. Can we -- can Mr. Hannis establish whether this document, what is the date of this document? Does this document actually refers to 1992 or some other time in the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I already indicated that the document itself indicated that it was processed on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it doesn't say which year. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Given where the locations are, and the sniper activity ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hannis, with all due respect, we had -- with had the trial of Sarajevo for the -- for the period of time between 1992 and 1995, and there has been allegations about the snipers and everything else during the whole period of war in Sarajevo. So, therefore, I don't think -- I'm pretty sure, actually, that this document does not refer to 1992 at all. That is -- that is the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, that objection should have been made when the document came into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just trying to find out whether this document was offered or it was introduced through a package or some other way. But I'm trying to find the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zecevic, save for the witness being assisted, in terms of the greater precision as to the date of this document, it is by whatever means already before the Tribunal so Mr. Hannis should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The last sentence in paragraph 4 about morale says: "Paramilitary formations that are still not disarmed are causing big problems. They behave more violently and are arrogant. Disarming these formations will not possible without armed clashes with them, especially since they are supported and established by certain organs in the local authorities and the police." Isn't that true that some of these paramilitary formations were supported by the municipal Crisis Staff or the SDS and/or the police in some of the municipalities in the Republika Srpska in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first say that if the document is from 1992, I wasn't in Sarajevo on 18 August. On the other hand, I can't help wondering, because it says Major-General.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, but if you could focus on my question. My question is: Is that statement there true? Isn't it true that in 1992, in various municipalities throughout Republika Srpska, that there were paramilitary formations that were supported by the local authorities, Crisis Staffs, and/or by the local police? That was the situation in some municipalities in the Republika Srpska in 1992, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether the police was supporting paramilitaries or took part in the creation of such units, is something I don't know. And that's why I am surprised to read the words of a major-general to make such a general statement. One would expect more precision from such a high-ranking officer, such as the police from Nedzarici or the police from Ilidza, that would be more precise. But some Crisis Staffs, some police organisations, all that makes me wonder. I don't know what to say about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question. Are you saying -- you just didn't know of that -- you didn't know of that happening in any municipality in Republika Srpska in 1992? Is that your answer? You weren't aware of any local -- any paramilitary being supported by the local authorities, Crisis Staff, or the local police? Never heard of that happening? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police supporting paramilitaries, no. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Crisis Staffs did, where I was involved and had information, I mean, where I was involved in breaking up these paramilitaries, to what extent the Crisis Staff of Zvornik supported the Yellow Wasps or whatever those people in Teslic were called or anywhere else, that is a segment I didn't deal with being in my administration. Receiving information from a centre chief that they had problems because some Crisis Staff was supporting a paramilitary unit is something else, but those paramilitary units were part of the army. So what exactly is supported? Is it the army or some unit that had broken loose? That's how I look at paramilitary units. I am not aware of such renegade units being supported by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You asked for some more precision. Let's go back to P591. Tab 96. This is Mr. Tolimir's report, Colonel Tolimir's report. I only showed you the first page, but in light of your comments, I think I need to show you one more. Do you still have the hard copy of that? That's the one that has -- it's dated the 28th of July, 1992. Information on paramilitary formations. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could go to your page 3 in B/C/S at the bottom. No, I'm sorry, I think I misinformed you. It's your page 5. English page 4 at the bottom. Your page 5. And it's the second bullet point down: "Serbian defence forces SOS from Banja Luka ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Serbian defence forces SOS from Banja Luka under the command of Nenad Stevandic, who was also president of the Serbian Sokol Society, private businessmen and some senior SJB and SNB officials in the Banja Luka CSB have considerable influence over the SOS, but many infamous Banja Luka criminals have joined the SOS. Part of the SOS formations joined the Banja Luka CSB special police detachment, but it's not really under either the control of the detachment's command or the CSB. Som SDS members have joined the Banja Luka TO." Doesn't that show that the local police and local officials are supporting one of these paramilitary formations in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may read it, because I haven't seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mean you want to read the whole document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, you have an interjection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have the same objection as put forward by Mr. Zecevic earlier. The witness gave evidence that he hadn't seen this document before. Now Mr. Hannis is reading something to him, and the witness said that he had no information about any municipality. Or perhaps the witness should remove his headphones. [In English] Yeah, but I'm talking in Serbian, so it is the same. [Interpretation] To cut a long story short, the same objection, the witness hasn't seen the document, and he said earlier that he didn't have any information. Now Mr. Hannis is reading something out to him and asking him, "Do you agree?" But the witness has already said that he didn't have any particular information and that includes SOS in Banja Luka. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I note your objection, Mr. Aleksic, but isn't the position that counsel, in this case from the OTP, has a witness on the stand, and he -- who is testifying generally about matters which are dealt with -- which have been dealt with in this case through a document. Admittedly, the witness has explained that he hasn't seen this particular document before, but it seems to be perfectly permissible, as Mr. Hannis did with to the previous witness, to ask him to -- I'm trying to phrase it correctly because it would be improper for him to ask the witness to comment on what another witness has said. But for -- for his -- understanding of the same events. If you understand that balance that Mr. Hannis I'm sure is aware that he has to strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I dealt with it because the witness said he was unaware of any municipality where that was the situation, and I was trying to show him where there was an example to see if that might refresh his memory. All right. Your Honours, I see it is 12.43. Might this be an appropriate time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If this is convenient for everyone, we may as well break now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know you indicated that I should finish my cross-examination in the course of day. I'm still hoping to do so. Depending on how well I'm able to phrase my questions and get short answers, I -- I hope to do so. If not, I may find myself in the position of requesting 15 additional minutes tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So noted, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, I want to ask you if, in 1992, you received any information about crimes being committed by policemen in Foca? Specifically, policemen who were guarding non-Serb detainees in Foca. Did you or your inspectors ever become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that, in 1992, I received any information about members of the police committing a crime. May I put this document aside, please, the military one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, you may. Did you, in watching proceedings at this Tribunal, never see the proceedings regarding Foca, where there were allegations against police in Foca, among others, having committed a sexual assault against female detainees in Foca? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't watch regularly. I would just happen to see a snap-shot or two sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In September 1992, where were you living and working? Were you still in Pale? Were you in Bijeljina yet; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both. On the 3rd of September, the whole team that worked on the Yellow Wasps case returned. In September, we were at a collegium meeting, after which we went back to Pale. Preparations were in progress in September to relocate the HQ of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing about the murders of three Muslim families in Bijeljina on about the 25th of September, 1992? It was, as I understand, highly publicised in the municipality. Did you learn about that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I was in Pale at the time. It was sometime in October that we returned to Bijeljina. The murder of these three families, I'm not sure if they were all murdered at the same time or at various intervals.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that this all happened on one night, about the 25th of September. And Mr. Blagojevic from the Serbian Radicals published something in the local media, suggesting that the crimes had been committed by Dusko Malovic's unit from the MUP. And you're telling us you never heard about that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When the administration arrived Bijeljina and when it was set up there, it received no information concerning the murder of these three families during the same night, as you suggest. I only met Mr. Blagojevic in mid-1993 -- rather, not met, not personally. I learned of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You never heard about it from Tomo Kovac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who was the head of state security at Bijeljina CSB in September 1992? Vukovic? Vuckovic, something like that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Drago Vukovic or perhaps someone else. State security, the boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you never heard from him about these murders either? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, state security?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you've personally have never been interviewed by anybody from the prosecutor's office in connection with your knowledge, if any, about that event?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. I think the total number of persons killed was somewhere between 20 and 30. That still doesn't ring a bell. Sejmenovic and Sarajlic are the names of two of the families.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned the family name of Sarajlic, I know about that from the media. I learned about that in the media two or three years ago, the Sarajlic case being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you about Koricanske Stijene. When was the first time you heard about the killing of 150 to 200 non-Serbs in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If memory serves, at the time we were preparing for our move to Bijeljina, and when I drew up that list, I was gathering some information. I can't say this with absolute certainty, but I think I saw some dispatches by the minister and was there a reference there to the murder of hundreds of Muslims or Croats, and I read the instructions and that he gave, or, rather, his response to that event. It wasn't before the first trimester in Banja Luka that I was informed by the leading men in the crime unit about what had occurred at Koricanske Stijene and also about what measures had been taken following that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. We have information in the case, I think it's Exhibit P2303, at pages 3 to 5, for counsel's reference, that Mr. Stanisic knew about this two or three days after it happened. Wouldn't he have informed you, given your position as head of the crime police administration, of an event as significant as this one?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you know, I was in Bijeljina at the time with specific missions there. I was coordinating all of the operative work there. It wasn't until after the event, because the centre probably hadn't informed me about the event, that I had a chance to respond to an event as momentous as that. I think it wasn't before I arrived in Pale on the 3rd of September, when we started our preparations, that I saw the dispatch by the minister containing specific instructions and a response to the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can the witness -- because none of his answer was properly recorded, can he be instructed to talk slowly because what we are getting in the transcript is not what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Certainly not what he said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer. Because you're recorded as having said when you arrived in Pale on the 3rd of September, "I saw the dispatch by the minister." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I think that that the first I learnt about the event was during our preparations for the move from Pale. This was the first time I saw a dispatch sent by Mr. Minister to the public security centre in Banja Luka with the adequate response to the event. As you know, the reporting system between October and as late as November did not go from the centre stations to the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm just trying to be clear now. I had understood you to say last week that the first time you heard about the Koricanske Stijene case was in March of 1993. Now you're telling me about it -- you knew about it in, what, September 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said it the last time around. Information on the event, and then it wasn't before March that I had an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Maybe we're not understanding each other. I'm trying to find out when was the first time you personally had any information, orally or in writing, about this crime at Koricanske Stijene that happened around the 20th, 21st of August, 1992? Did you find out it in 1992 or not until 1993? I'm not saying full information. When was the first time you heard anything about it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the event, meaning, as I said a while ago, I think it was in September 1992; information that an event like that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how did you find that out? Were you told personally by somebody, or did you see a document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the preparations for the move and while gathering information, I saw a document sent by the minister to the public security centre, or, rather, the -- the communique. Specifically, I remember a document, the dispatch, sent by the minister to the public security centre with certain instructions that were more of a response to a serious event, and the public security centre knew how to act on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's show you Exhibit P847. This is tab 128.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is one that I just added this morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I would hand you a hard copy but my hard copy is not very legible. And I don't know if e-court is any better. That's not it yet. Yes, the B/C/S copy is not very legible. But I tell you, an English translation was made apparently by somebody working from a better copy. Perhaps the original from the evidence vault. And it's dated the 31st of August, 1992, from Mico Stanisic to the chief in Banja Luka CSB, ordering him "to conduct a full investigation regarding the deaths of 150 Muslims in the territory of the municipality of Skender Vakuf at Koricanske Stijene." Is this the dispatch you were talking about; and do you think this is the one? Sounds like you were describing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see what it says. But I think it was a longer text than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you if it would be -- well, what was the procedure? Was there a role for you in a case like this; or did you just simply sit back and wait for something to be done by your administration in the CSB? This seems like a big case, and it seems like it would be something that the minister would involve you in; but maybe I'm wrong in assuming that.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister responded in keeping with his function. Public security stations and the public security stations [as interpreted] operate in keeping with the Law on Criminal Procedure and the Criminal Code. And the -- at the end of it all, it is my opinion that the Banja Luka centre had much better men at its disposal than I did, the seven or eight people that I had over at the crime police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was one of those persons a Brane Buhovac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean was one of those persons Brane Buhovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what I mean. Was he one of those persons in CSB Sarajevo that was better for the job than people that worked for you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brane Buhovac was an employee of the Banja Luka CSB. I didn't know the gentleman at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I understood your answer to be that, in your opinion, the Banja Luka centre had better men at its disposal to work on this case. And my question was: Is Brane Buhovac one of those better men at the CSB that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know Mr. Buhovac; therefore, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. How about Milivoje Pavicic? Was he one of the Banja Luka guys you were referring to that was better than your guys to work on this case?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me remind you: The men who, at the beginning, constituted the crime police administration did not include anyone from the forensic centre in Sarajevo. Or, indeed, at the any of the lower levels. The names that you mentioned are names I know from later periods when we started to establish a forensic centre over in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand now. Could I show you tab 129. This is Exhibit 2D35. And, Mr. Macar, with the usher's help, I will hand you a hard copy of this. Well, maybe I won't. I don't seem to have the hard copy. So if you could look at the screen, it's dated the 8th of September, 1992, from Stojan Zupljanin, chief of the CSB, to the public prosecutor's office in Banja Luka. Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember directly that I held in my hand and read it. I think the gentleman who was in -- the boss of the crime service, Mr. Tegeltija, reported on the case file and there was probably the criminal report too. Sometime in March 1993. I can't remember the exact date but it was during that trimester.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In terms of internal MUP procedure, would you and your administration in headquarters be advised or receive a copy of a criminal report like this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After arriving in Bijeljina and setting up the ministry HQ, once the visits began to the centres and stations, and once the technical conditions were created in Bijeljina for communication, in technical terms, and then it started in earnest in 1993 informing by way of dispatches about the event. As for the MUP, the administration at the HQ, as of 1993 on, I can't be specific about the date when this system of reporting got off the ground, it was then that we started reporting cases and any criminal reports that were filed. But those were never forwarded to the Ministry of the Interior, not until 1992 or, indeed, after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll -- let me show you another document, then. This is P800. It's tab 126. If the usher could assist. This is dated the 22nd of September, 1992, from the department chief, Zoran Josic in the crime prevention and detection department in Banja Luka. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the boss of the crime service, the Banja Luka SJB department.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is entitled "Reminder about the provisions on instruction of -- on urgent reporting." And according to that instruction, it says: "It is obligatory for public security stations to submit urgent reports to the ministry ... and to the CSB on important security-related events and occurrences." And then farther down you will see at the top of the list the kinds that must be reported is murder and attempted murder, Article 36. So at least according to this instruction, in -- in the SJB in Sarajevo, this is the kind of thing that should be reported up to the CSB and the MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the tasks. So up until 1992, there was the instruction on urgent, current, and occasional reporting in the bodies of the Ministry of the Interior. But I pointed out on numerous occasions what the problems were because of shortage of technology and equipment in the stations, centres, and even the ministry itself, so that the instruction could never become operational until the basic conditions were in place, which was in October 1992. Not just at the ministry HQ but also on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have explained already, if I may just finish. As I've explained already, working by courier is something that perhaps saved my life. Regrettably, though, in Doboj, sometime in July 1992, we wanted to have better communication and we dispatched a single engineer who was killed on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please stop. In September of 1992, the communications between Banja Luka CSB and the headquarters and Banja Luka CSB and Banja Luka SJB were fully functional, weren't they? The corridor had been opened at the end of June or beginning of July. But my question wasn't about the technical problems. My question was whether this instruction was such that this kind of thing should have been reported up to MUP headquarters in September 1992. Would you agree or not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: An instruction that couldn't be implemented for a single period, although we had it until 1992, and then we more or less copied it and had this new one after 1992, could not be implemented in practice, just as many other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Stop, please. It could have been implemented by a courier even if the other means of communication weren't working; right? It could have been. Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the Sarajevo centre --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please. Please, Mr. Macar --

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- used a courier service a lot --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- I'm really giving up hope on finishing with you today if you can't answer a question yes or no. Please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were war-time conditions, and I really cannot comment whether a courier service could be set up over a distance of 300 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if I were to see a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you saying Mr. Stanisic's dispatch that we just looked at telling Mr. Zupljanin to investigate this case, are you saying that didn't get communicated, that didn't get through? That's not what you're claiming, is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that isn't what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about Exhibit P1567. This is tab 118. This is a very thick document. I want to go to English page 52, and B/C/S page 43. Now, Mr. Buhovac, you know, was a forensic guy in Banja Luka CSB in 1992; right? You know that.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I get the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's on the screen. But, first, can you answer my question: You know that Mr. Buhovac was a forensic worker at Banja Luka CSB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember his exact position. I tend to think that he was a chief of the forensic section.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before? It's an Official Note taken of Mr. Buhovac in October 1999 about the investigation in connection with Koricanske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And no one ever told you before that at one point in time, specifically 1999, Mr. Buhovac had made a claim which he later withdrew, you should know. But in 1999, in this Official Note, he said: "As for the videotape of the scene ..." This is on the last page, if we could go to page 44 in the B/C/S. Page 56 in e-court in the English, at the last -- last page, right before he says, "This is all I have to say." He says: "As for the videotape of the scene, I can tell you it has been erased using a VCR on the order of the UKP chief, Goran Macar."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you -- I can't find what you are reading from in the document which is P1567. 1567 is a set of documents concerning the Koricanske Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm looking at that in e-court, page 43 of a 60-some page document in e-court. And English starts at page 52 of a longer document. Am I incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. But I don't see it -- I don't see it on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Should be on the screen in both English and B/C/S at the correct page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll check it out. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No one ever told you about that claim by Mr. Buhovac? Never heard about it until just now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not before you told me about it. But what I can say before looking at the document is that this is a blatant lie and I cannot believe that Mr. Buhovac stated anything like that. I would really like to see the document to see the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's all he says, what you see on the screen right there. That's the only context. But I will tell you that later, years later, in July of 2003, in a witness statement to the -- to our office, to the Prosecutor's office, he said: "The sentence that says that Goran Macar" -- I'm reading from page 6 of the witness statement of 27 July 2003 from Mr. Buhovac, which may be part of his 92 quater, I believe, but I don't have that exhibit number. The sentence that states -- paragraph 16: "The sentence that states that Goran Macar ordered me to erase this tape is incorrect. I never had a conversation with him about this tape. I actually called Goran Macar and told him that I did not have the means to safe-guard the tape and that someone might steal it. Since the original tape was in the possession of the inspector, I did not want to have the responsibility of having the second tape in my possession. I decided to erase this tape and I think Pavicic is the one that actually erased the tape, and I think there is some sort of record about that." You never heard about this either, I take it. Since you didn't hear about the original claim that you had something to do with it, so I assume you never heard about Mr. Buhovac withdrawing that claim; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state with full responsibility that what you have just said and what this Official Note says -- and it's interesting that there is no material for me to see. Some officials made a note, and it says: "As for the videotape of the scene, I can tell that you it has been erased using a VCR on the order of the UKP chief, Goran Macar." And that's all. Now the question is -- I can't believe that Mr. Buhovac really stated that. But it's interesting that none of these officials was interested enough to ask any questions, what, when, where, how. Because this allegation isn't anything that you should take lightly without additional verification. So I needn't continue. But I can't believe that Mr. Buhovac could have ever have said that. I'm certain that this is all wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You and I agree about asking more questions about that. I have a couple of minutes left today. Did you ever have any conversation with Mr. Pavicic about a videotape, in relation to Koricanske Stijene; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Mr. Pavicic. I think I remember that he was a forensic technician. I don't think I communicated with him. Whenever we needed forensic technicians, I communicated with Mr. Buhovac. And if I happened to meet any of his associates, it must have been at some meeting, possibly in 1994 or so. And as for the video cassette, I really have nothing to do with that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and I don't believe that Mr. Buhovac ever really stated that. Because there's no basis for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see it's about time to adjourn for the day. I think I do need 15 more minutes tomorrow, if I may. We did have a late start today and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I remind everyone that we reconvene at 9.30 tomorrow. So we take the adjournment now for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of July, 2011, at 9.30 a.m.
